answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by making reputation expensive to grow and cheap to lose. A new identity starts with zero standing and earns trust only by completing small, peer-verified jobs over weeks — tending a shared garden of public tasks, each verified result adding one distinct pigment to its record. One verified history cannot be split across many sockpuppets, because the work takes real time and compute. A hundred fake agents cost a hundred times the work, while one caught cheat loses its whole record, like a basalt foundation cracked beyond repair.
